findings.statement: range-partitioned compaction recovers the ordered-scan axis by at least 12x
findings.detail: compact-T4 scans 3060788 entries/s against the unrouted fan's 2356638 -- 1.3x (compact-T4 vs no-compact: greater 1.299x (p=0.0453, rel_iqr 15.1%/13.2%)), over 13 live segments against 7. EXT.24 measured the fan at 0.040x of LMDB, so 12x is what compaction-plan.md's P4.1 needs to reach the registered 0.5x; the ext-kv suite is where that claim is actually settled

findings.statement: fence-and-Bloom routing does not cost the read path
findings.detail: compact-T4 reads 2174225/s against the unrouted fan's 2158399 (compact-T4 vs no-compact: NO DIFFERENCE (ratio 1.007, p=0.6889) -- within noise, not a result). The fan probes every segment; the routed arm probes one partition plus a bounded Bloomed tail, which is the arithmetic F38.1 and F40.1 priced

findings.statement: compaction costs less than 2x the device bytes of never compacting
findings.detail: compact-T4 sent 8.6 MB to the device against 6.2 without compaction -- 1.39x, on disk 4.1 MB against 4.0. Every merge rewrites what it touches, so this is the write amplification the tail bound buys the read path with

findings.statement: compaction does not slow the durable load path
findings.detail: compact-T4 loads 296351 ops/s against 406178 without compaction (compact-T4 vs no-compact: less 0.730x (p=0.0122, rel_iqr 7.1%/3.4%)). The merge runs on a background thread and the commit path never waits on it; a regression here convicts the backpressure, not the merge

notes: three arms interleaved in one process, fresh store per rep: no-compact keeps every segment in the unrouted L0 fan (milestone 3 exactly), compact-T4 and compact-T8 merge the tail into disjoint fence-routed partitions at two tail bounds. Load, then reads, then ordered scans, all over the store the arm just built

seal_bytes is set small so a full-profile load produces enough segments to compact several times; the absolute throughputs are therefore not comparable with f42, whose seal threshold is the shipping default. The comparison here is between arms
predictions registered in compaction-plan.md before the merge was written
